discussion_comments.comment_body: Consider placing ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID first in precedence, for users that want both Gemini and Anthropic models via Vertex AI but with different projects.

Thanks for the feedback, what you propose does make sense, however this precedence order was taken from [Anthropic's docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/google-vertex-ai#3-configure-gcp-credentials) describing the precedence of these env vars Claude Code:

> Claude Code uses `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID` as the project ID for Vertex AI requests. The `GCLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` environment variables and the credential file referenced by `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` take precedence over it. If none of these are set, the project ID is resolved from your gcloud configuration or the attached service account.

Of course, we don't have to follow Claude Code's precedence, but then there's the edge case where users that have both env vars set to different values will get different GCP projects being used between Pi and Claude Code.

Maybe it's true when this PR was originally written, but as of 2026-07-20 Bedrock Mantle are available in a lot more regions (see [Region availability by endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints-region-availability.html)). I think we should allow this region to be configurable.

Bedrock Mantle is available in much more regions but OpenAI models are still available only in a few US regions, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-region-compatibility.html#model-regions-openai.

I've updated to use `https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION}.api.aws/openai/v1"` as the `baseUrl` and also added hardcoded region availability per-model for now - I think ideally that should be coming from models.dev: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/6216/commits/a4bbfd21ad6a574ff734e4efd51c68235997905e

Please make this configurable :-) I rebind `ctrl+n` in session picker for "select down". Here's part of my keybindings:
```
  "selectUp": ["up", "ctrl+p"],
  "selectDown": ["down", "ctrl+n"],
```
These are just standard Emacs/readline keybindings btw
Let's not make this a nested propert. quietStartup on Settings is fine.
Done. It was nested because I initially added a flag to hide every little thing separately. That didn't make much sense, so I ended up with just one flag and a nested struct :upside_down_face:

The idea to have a custom convertToLlm is right, the implementation is wrong. createAgentSession is called once per session. If the settings.json has blockImages:true, then images will always be filtered for the remainder of the session, even if the user changes the setting mid session via /settings. This needs to evaluate sessionmanager.getBlockImages() and only filter, if that's true.
